subject: #848 MCP inline email auth (anonymous MCP session tier + /api/internal/mcp-auth/*)

attack_surface.new_outbound_http: 4 internalFetch calls, fixed literal paths, config baseUrl (no user-controlled host)
attack_surface.widened_trust: INTERNAL_API_SECRET can now act as any verified email via /chat + /playbooks (flag-gated, default off)

accepted_risk_notes.title: INTERNAL_API_SECRET widened to act as any verified email
accepted_risk_notes.detail: The /chat and /playbooks endpoints let a caller holding the internal secret dispatch chat / list playbooks as any email that passes email_has_agent_access. This is the mechanism option A requires. It grants NO privilege beyond internal-secret compromise, which already gates all of /api/internal/* (backend god-mode). Gated behind MCP_INLINE_AUTH_ENABLED (default OFF) and the internal secret (network-internal). Documented in the PR. Note the pre-existing INTERNAL_API_SECRET -> SECRET_KEY fallback (routers/internal.py:42): the widened surface is another reason to set INTERNAL_API_SECRET explicitly in production rather than rely on the fallback.
accepted_risk_notes.action: Accepted design. No code change required. Keep the flag off unless sharing agents with external users; set INTERNAL_API_SECRET explicitly.

accepted_risk_notes.title: Inline /verify shares the per-account login bucket (pre-existing, targeted DoS only)
accepted_risk_notes.detail: check_login_rate_limit_account_only uses login_attempts_acct:{email} (LOGIN_ACCOUNT_LIMIT=5), the same bucket the web login path already increments. 5 bad inline codes for a known email can 429 that email's web login for 15 min. Pre-existing property of the shared account bucket; #848 adds no new capability. DoS-class, hard-excluded.
